option_description: Attests that tokens/credentials on this untrusted device live exclusively in the OS-protected, ideally hardware-backed keystore (iOS Keychain/Secure Enclave, Android Keystore/StrongBox, or EncryptedSharedPreferences) rather than in plaintext SharedPreferences, NSUserDefaults, plist, SQLite, or sandbox files.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Insecure local credential/token storage" — fires when hardware_backed_credential_storage_used is false (is_false), meaning credentials are recoverable from a lost, stolen, or rooted device (ATT&CK T1552.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Statically/dynamically review where the app persists tokens/credentials and confirm exclusive use of the OS keystore.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: Android keys created via Android Keystore (KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore")), preferably with setIsStrongBoxBacked(true) where available, and secrets stored via EncryptedSharedPreferences/Jetpack Security. iOS secrets in Keychain via SecItemAdd. Insecure: secrets found in SharedPreferences XML, NSUserDefaults, plist, plaintext SQLite, or app sandbox files.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On iOS, confirm Keychain items carry the most restrictive accessibility class consistent with function.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: iOS Keychain items carry the most restrictive accessibility class consistent with function — kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly (not ...Always / not synced to iCloud) for tokens that should never leave the device.

option_description: Positive interpreted boolean — true when tokens, session credentials, or secrets are observed persisted in cleartext in app-readable device storage (SharedPreferences XML, NSUserDefaults, plist, plaintext SQLite, caches, or sandbox files) outside the keystore.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Insecure local credential/token storage" — fires when tokens_in_plaintext_device_storage is true (is_true); polarity-safe positive boolean so the secure baseline stays silent (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Examine app-readable storage on a test/rooted device for any cleartext token/credential/secret persisted outside the keystore.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: Android keys created via Android Keystore (KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore")), preferably with setIsStrongBoxBacked(true) where available, and secrets stored via EncryptedSharedPreferences/Jetpack Security. iOS secrets in Keychain via SecItemAdd. Insecure (this attribute true): secrets found in SharedPreferences XML, NSUserDefaults, plist, plaintext SQLite, or app sandbox files.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Static/dynamic review of the app sandbox for cleartext PII/tokens in caches, databases, logs, or WebView local storage.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Static/dynamic review of the app sandbox finds no cleartext PII/tokens in caches, databases, logs, or WebView local storage; sensitive blobs are AES-GCM encrypted under a keystore-held key. This attribute is true when any cleartext token/secret IS found.

option_description: Attests that sensitive data (PII, tokens, secrets) persisted on the device outside the keystore is encrypted at rest with a keystore-held key (e.g. AES-GCM under a Keystore key), rather than written as cleartext caches/logs/temp files/WebView storage.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Insecure local credential/token storage" — fires when encrypted_at_rest is false (is_false), i.e. cleartext sensitive data is present at rest (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Static/dynamic review of the app sandbox confirming sensitive data persisted outside the keystore is encrypted with a Keystore/Keychain-held key.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Static/dynamic review of the app sandbox finds no cleartext PII/tokens in caches, databases, logs, or WebView local storage; sensitive blobs are AES-GCM encrypted under a keystore-held key.

option_description: Attests all app-to-backend traffic is carried over TLS only, with cleartext transport impossible (Android Network Security Config cleartextTrafficPermitted=false / iOS App Transport Security left on, NSAllowsArbitraryLoads not set).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Cleartext transport / no certificate pinning" — fires when tls_only_transport is false (is_false), letting the channel fall back to cleartext HTTP for MITM (ATT&CK T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Android Network Security Config for cleartextTrafficPermitted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" in <base-config> (also the Android 9 / API 28+ default). Insecure: cleartextTrafficPermitted="true". Config must be wired in via android:networkSecurityConfig on the <application> element in AndroidManifest.xml.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the iOS Info.plist App Transport Security keys.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: NSAppTransportSecurity has NO NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true and no broad NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads exceptions (ATS on by default since iOS 9 SDK, enforces HTTPS/TLS 1.2+). Insecure: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads = true.

option_description: Interpreted boolean over the composite transport-trust config (Android cleartextTrafficPermitted, iOS NSAllowsArbitraryLoads / NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads): true when the app is configured to permit cleartext HTTP to the backend or a broad insecure-HTTP exception.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Cleartext transport / no certificate pinning" — fires when cleartext_http_permitted is true (is_true), letting the hostile-device adversary read/alter the channel (ATT&CK T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Android Network Security Config for any cleartext-permitting setting.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" (this attribute false). Insecure (this attribute true): cleartextTrafficPermitted="true" or a per-domain cleartext exception.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the iOS Info.plist for NSAllowsArbitraryLoads or broad insecure-HTTP exceptions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: no NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true and no broad NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads. Insecure (this attribute true): NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true or NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads set.

option_description: Attests the app pins the backend's certificate/public key (Android <pin-set> SHA-256 SPKI pins with a backup pin; iOS URLSession delegate / pinning lib), so a malicious CA or user-installed root on a compromised/rooted device cannot transparently MITM the channel.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Cleartext transport / no certificate pinning" — fires when certificate_pinning_enabled is false (is_false), leaving the app on system trust only so a user-installed root CA can intercept TLS (ATT&CK T1557, T1553.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Android Network Security Config for a <pin-set> on the backend domain.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: <domain-config> for the backend host contains a <pin-set> with at least two <pin digest="SHA-256"> SPKI hashes (current + backup) and <trust-anchors> not silently trusting user CAs. Insecure: no pin-set, or <certificates src="user"/> trusted in production.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On iOS, confirm pinning is implemented in the URLSession delegate or a pinning library for backend connections (no dossier command exists for the iOS path).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: backend connections pin the server certificate or public key via URLSession:didReceiveChallenge: validation or a pinning library, with a backup pin. Insecure: system trust only, no pinning.

option_description: Attests the mobile client fully validates the backend server certificate chain (no disabled hostname verification, no trust-all/accept-any TrustManager or insecure URLSession delegate).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Cleartext transport / no certificate pinning" — fires when server_certificate_validated is false (is_false), where any presented certificate is accepted enabling trivial MITM (ATT&CK T1557).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Android Network Security Config trust-anchors / certificate sources for the backend domain.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: <trust-anchors> use only <certificates src="system"/> (plus explicit pinned CAs); overridePins absent/false. Insecure: <certificates src="user"/> present, or overridePins="true".

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the app code for any trust-all/accept-any TrustManager, disabled hostname verification, or insecure URLSession delegate (no dossier command isolates this).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: no custom TrustManager that returns without validation, no HostnameVerifier that always returns true, no URLSession delegate calling completionHandler with .useCredential unconditionally. Insecure: chain validation bypassed.

option_description: Interpreted boolean — true when the app detects a rooted/jailbroken runtime and gates or restricts sensitive flows on a positive verdict (defence-in-depth).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "No jailbreak/root detection or app-integrity attestation" — fires when root_jailbreak_detection_enabled is false (is_false), so the app runs identically on a rooted/jailbroken device, silently undermining OS sandbox guarantees that protect the keystore and screen.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review whether the app performs root/jailbreak checks and gates/limits sensitive flows on a positive verdict.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: app performs root/jailbreak checks and gates/limits sensitive flows on a positive verdict (defence-in-depth, not sole control). Insecure: app runs identically on a rooted/jailbroken device with no check or response.

option_description: Interpreted boolean — true when the backend server-side verifies the request comes from a genuine, untampered instance of the real app on a genuine device (Android Play Integrity deviceIntegrity/appLicensingVerdict; iOS App Attest DCAppAttestService assertion validated server-side) and the app resists tampering/repackaging.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for TWO exposures — "No jailbreak/root detection or app-integrity attestation" and "App repackaging & hardcoded-secret extraction" — each firing when server_verified_app_integrity_attestation is false (is_false), where the server trusts any client claiming to be the app and a repackaged forged app is indistinguishable from the genuine one (ATT&CK T1036.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the backend validates an Android Play Integrity verdict server-side before trusting a request.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: backend validates a Play Integrity verdict (deviceIntegrity contains MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY and/or MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY; appLicensingVerdict = LICENSED) and/or an iOS App Attest assertion server-side, rejecting/elevating-friction on failure. Insecure: server trusts any client claiming to be the app.
how_to_obtain.source: Google Play Integrity API — verdicts (Android Developers)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the iOS path uses App Attest with server-side validation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: iOS: app calls DCAppAttestService to generate a Secure-Enclave keypair and the server validates the Apple-signed attestation object / assertions; private key never leaves the Secure Enclave.

option_description: True when long-lived API keys, signing secrets, or backend shared secrets are embedded in the app binary/resources (APK/IPA) or bundled config rather than provisioned at runtime over an authenticated channel.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "App repackaging & hardcoded-secret extraction" — fires when secrets_hardcoded_in_config_or_iac is true (is_true), since an attacker decompiles the package and recovers the secret by string/entropy analysis (ATT&CK T1036.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Decompile the APK/IPA and run static analysis / string + entropy scanning over binary, resources, and bundled config.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: static analysis / string + entropy scan of the decompiled APK/IPA finds no long-lived API keys, private keys, or backend secrets; any per-device secret is provisioned at runtime over the authenticated channel. Insecure (this attribute true): secrets recoverable from the binary.

option_description: Lifetime of the mobile session's access token in minutes. Short-lived tokens bound the replay window of a token stolen off a lost or compromised device; long-lived tokens let a stolen bearer token be replayed until expiry.
security_impact: One of the AND/OR conditions for the exposure "Long-lived bearer token theft and replay" — fires when access_token_ttl_minutes is greater than 60 (gt 60), making a stolen token replayable for a long window (ATT&CK T1528, T1550.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the access-token lifetime from the authorization server / token issuance config and express it in minutes (the dossier frames token TTL as a server-side OAuth attestation, not a single device command).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: short access-token TTL (minutes), refresh-token rotation with reuse-detection, and DPoP (RFC 9449) or mTLS (RFC 8705) binding tokens to the device key. Insecure: long-lived plain bearer tokens accepted from any client. The exposure fires when TTL exceeds 60 minutes.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 9700 — OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice

option_description: Whether the access token is sender-constrained (bound to the device's key via DPoP per RFC 9449 or mTLS per RFC 8705) rather than a plain bearer token replayable verbatim.
security_impact: One of the conditions for the exposure "Long-lived bearer token theft and replay" — fires when sender_constrained is false (is_false), so a token exfiltrated from device storage/logs can be replayed verbatim from attacker hardware (ATT&CK T1550.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm access tokens are bound to the device key via DPoP (RFC 9449) or mTLS (RFC 8705).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: short access-token TTL (minutes), refresh-token rotation with reuse-detection, and DPoP (RFC 9449) or mTLS (RFC 8705) binding tokens to the device key. Insecure: long-lived plain bearer tokens accepted from any client.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 9700 — OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice

option_description: Whether refresh tokens are rotated on use with reuse-detection (RFC 9700). Without rotation a stolen refresh token mints fresh access tokens indefinitely and replay goes undetected.
security_impact: One of the conditions for the exposure "Long-lived bearer token theft and replay" — fires when refresh_token_rotation_enabled is false (is_false) (ATT&CK T1528).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm refresh tokens are rotated on each use and reuse of a retired token is detected and triggers revocation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: short access-token TTL (minutes), refresh-token rotation with reuse-detection, and DPoP (RFC 9449) or mTLS (RFC 8705) binding tokens to the device key. Insecure: long-lived plain bearer tokens accepted from any client.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 9700 — OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice

option_description: Whether the backend exposes a server-side revocation/logout path that immediately invalidates a device's access and refresh tokens (e.g. on reported device loss/theft).
security_impact: One of the conditions for the exposure "Long-lived bearer token theft and replay" — fires when server_side_revocation_supported is false (is_false), so stolen-token access persists until natural expiry with no recovery (ATT&CK T1528).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a server-side revocation/logout endpoint exists that immediately invalidates a device's access+refresh tokens on demand and the app supports remote/local wipe.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: a server-side revocation/logout endpoint invalidates the device's access+refresh tokens immediately, and the app supports remote/local wipe of stored secrets. Insecure: revoked only by waiting for token expiry; no app-data wipe.

option_description: Attests sensitive data (tokens, credentials, PII) is excluded from OS/cloud device backups — Android android:allowBackup="false" or backup/dataExtractionRules excluding secret stores, and iOS Keychain items using a ...ThisDeviceOnly accessibility class.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Sensitive data leakage via backups, logs, clipboard, screen capture" — fires when excluded_from_device_backup is false (is_false), so secrets ride into backups and leak to an attacker who restores/harvests them (ATT&CK T1115).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the AndroidManifest for allowBackup (and dataExtractionRules/fullBackupContent).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: android:allowBackup="false" (or fullBackupContent/dataExtractionRules excluding secret stores). Insecure: allowBackup="true" with secrets in backed-up paths. iOS: secrets use ...ThisDeviceOnly Keychain accessibility so they are never written to iCloud backups.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On iOS, confirm device-bound secrets use a ...ThisDeviceOnly Keychain accessibility class so they are never written to iCloud/iTunes backups.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: iOS Keychain items carry the most restrictive accessibility class consistent with function — kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly (not ...Always / not synced to iCloud) for tokens that should never leave the device.

option_description: Attests sensitive screens block screenshots/screen-recording and resist overlay/tapjacking — Android FLAG_SECURE on sensitive windows (plus filterTouchesWhenObscured), and iOS hides/blurs sensitive content in the app-switcher snapshot.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Sensitive data leakage via backups, logs, clipboard, screen capture" — fires when screen_capture_protection_enabled is false (is_false), so sensitive screens are freely screenshot/recorded/overlaid (ATT&CK T1115).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm sensitive Activities set FLAG_SECURE and use overlay protection; iOS blurs/hides content in the app-switcher snapshot.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: sensitive Activities set WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE (screenshots blocked / recordings show black); overlay protection via filterTouchesWhenObscured; iOS blurs/hides content in the app-switcher snapshot. Insecure: sensitive screens freely screenshot/recorded.
how_to_obtain.source: Android — Secure sensitive activities / FLAG_SECURE (Android Developers)

option_description: Attests secret-entry fields enforce clipboard/keyboard hygiene — secrets are not auto-copied to the shared clipboard and secret fields use secure/no-suggestion input types (iOS isSecureTextEntry / autocorrectionType=.no; Android inputType textNoSuggestions/textPassword).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Sensitive data leakage via backups, logs, clipboard, screen capture" — fires when sensitive_clipboard_hygiene is false (is_false), so passwords/tokens land on the shared clipboard or keyboard cache readable by other apps (ATT&CK T1115).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm secret-entry fields use secure/no-suggestion input types and secrets are not auto-copied to the clipboard.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: secret entry fields set secure/no-suggestion input types (iOS isSecureTextEntry / autocorrectionType=.no; Android inputType textNoSuggestions/textPassword) and secrets are not auto-copied to the clipboard. Insecure: passwords/tokens cached by the keyboard or copied to a long-lived clipboard.

option_description: Attests credentials, tokens, and PII are excluded/masked from device logs (logcat / NSLog / crash-reporting SDKs) and debug logging is stripped from release builds.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Sensitive data leakage via backups, logs, clipboard, screen capture" — fires when secrets_masked_in_logs is false (is_false), so secrets are written to device logs readable on a rooted device or harvested by crash services (CWE-532, ATT&CK T1115).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture device logs on a test device and grep for secrets at runtime; confirm release builds strip debug logging.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: no credentials/tokens/PII appear in device logs at any verbosity; debug logging stripped from release builds. Insecure: secrets visible in logcat/NSLog or shipped to a crash service.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE CWE-532 Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

option_description: Interpreted boolean — deep-link / custom-URL-scheme / intent handlers validate the origin and parameters of the inbound link and re-check authorization server-side before acting.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Malicious deep link & untrusted client-supplied data" — fires when deep_link_origin_validated is false (is_false), where a crafted link or intent drives a sensitive action or leaks data without checks (ATT&CK T1204.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review deep-link/custom-URL-scheme/intent handlers to confirm they validate origin+params and re-check authorization server-side.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: deep-link / intent handlers validate origin and parameters and re-check authorization server-side before acting; Android prefers verified App Links over custom schemes; exported components are minimized. Insecure: a crafted link/intent can drive sensitive actions or leak data without checks.

option_description: Enum over the deep-link/URL-scheme validation posture: 'validated_authorized' (handlers validate origin+params, prefer verified App Links, minimize exported components) vs 'unvalidated_deep_links' (a crafted link/intent triggers sensitive actions or leaks data without checks).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Malicious deep link & untrusted client-supplied data" — fires when deep_link_url_scheme_validation equals "unvalidated_deep_links" (eq) (ATT&CK T1204.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether inbound deep links/URL schemes/intents are validated and authorized, and classify the posture.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure ('validated_authorized'): deep-link / intent handlers validate origin and parameters and re-check authorization server-side before acting; Android prefers verified App Links over custom schemes; exported components are minimized. Insecure ('unvalidated_deep_links'): a crafted link/intent can drive sensitive actions or leak data without checks.

option_description: Interpreted boolean — the backend re-validates every request from the untrusted mobile client with allow-list input validation and authorization independent of any client-side gate.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Malicious deep link & untrusted client-supplied data" — fires when server_side_allowlist_validation is false (is_false), where the backend relies on client-supplied input being well-formed or on the app to enforce business rules (ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the backend re-validates every request with allow-list input validation and authorization, independent of any client-side gate.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: server re-validates every request with allow-list input validation and authorization independent of any client-side gate; client-side jailbreak/integrity checks are advisory, with the server as authority. Insecure: backend trusts client-supplied flags or relies on the app to enforce business rules.

option_description: Interpreted boolean — whether the backend trusts client-asserted state (entitlements, prices, identifiers, geofence/jailbreak/integrity claims) supplied by the mobile app. The secure posture is false (client claims are advisory; the server is the authority).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Malicious deep link & untrusted client-supplied data" — fires when client_asserted_state_trusted_serverside is true (is_true), so a tampered or instrumented app bypasses enforcement (ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine whether the backend trusts client-asserted state (entitlements, prices, identifiers, geofence/jailbreak/integrity claims) or treats them as advisory only.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure (this attribute false): server re-validates every request independent of any client-side gate; client-side jailbreak/integrity checks are advisory, with the server as authority. Insecure (this attribute true): backend trusts client-supplied flags or relies on the app to enforce business rules.

option_description: Interpreted attestation — access to keystore-held secrets and sensitive in-app actions is gated behind a device biometric/local-auth challenge (Android BiometricPrompt before key use; iOS Keychain items with a biometry-bound SecAccessControl, e.g. .biometryCurrentSet).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Missing local-auth (biometric) gating of secrets" — fires when biometric_local_auth_gates_secrets is false (is_false), so secrets are usable with no challenge on a momentarily-unlocked or stolen device (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm access to keystore-held secrets and sensitive in-app actions requires a fresh biometric/local-auth challenge.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: Android keys created with setUserAuthenticationRequired(true) (BiometricPrompt before use); iOS Keychain items with biometry-bound access control (SecAccessControl, .biometryCurrentSet). Insecure: secrets usable with no local-auth challenge.

option_description: Interpreted attestation — keystore keys protecting secrets are cryptographically bound to user authentication so the OS will not release/use them without a fresh local-auth challenge (Android setUserAuthenticationRequired(true); iOS SecAccessControl with biometry/userPresence enforced by the Secure Enclave).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for the exposure "Missing local-auth (biometric) gating of secrets" — fires when keys_bound_to_user_authentication is false (is_false), leaving keys usable on a stolen unlocked device (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect how keystore keys are created to confirm they are auth-bound so the OS/Secure Enclave will not use them without a fresh local-auth challenge.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: Android keys created with setUserAuthenticationRequired(true) (BiometricPrompt before use); iOS Keychain items with biometry-bound access control (SecAccessControl, .biometryCurrentSet). Insecure: secrets usable with no local-auth challenge.
